description: Neovim plugin to visualize C/C++ class/struct memory layouts using clang

summary.one_liner: A Neovim plugin that shows C/C++ struct and class memory layouts (field offsets, padding, alignment) in a floating window, using clang.
summary.what_it_does: The plugin is triggered from the cursor position on a C or C++ type name or variable, via the ` cl` keymap or the :ClassLayout command. It resolves variables to their underlying type through clangd and then uses clang to compile the saved file and compute the type's layout. The result is shown in a floating window listing field offsets, padding and alignment. It handles structs, classes, unions and STL types, and reads compiler flags from compile_commands.json or compile_flags.txt when present. Results are cached, so repeat lookups are faster after the first compile. Press q to close the window.
use_cases: see where padding is wasted in a struct
check field offsets while writing C or C++ code
inspect the memory layout of a class without a debugger
find alignment problems in a data structure
view the layout of a variable's underlying type
compare struct layouts while editing in Neovim
how_to_run: Ensure clang is in PATH and clangd is available for variable type resolution
Optionally call require("classlayout").setup({ keymap = " cl", compiler = "clang", args = {}, compile_commands = true })
Open a C or C++ file, save it, and place the cursor on a type name or variable
Press q to close the floating window
notable: Resolves variables to their underlying type via clangd
Auto-detects flags from compile_commands.json or compile_flags.txt
Caches results so repeat lookups are instant
Works on structs, classes, unions and STL types
caveats: Requires clang in PATH and clangd for variable and qualified type resolution
Layout is based on the saved file on disk, so unsaved edits are not reflected; save before invoking
